promptLatex: A rhombus has diagonals of length $10$ and $24$. What is the area of the rhombus, in square units?
hintLatex: The diagonals of a rhombus meet at right angles and bisect each other.
Cutting along one diagonal leaves two congruent right triangles.
solutionLatex:
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so their intersection splits the rhombus into four congruent right triangles with legs $5$ and $12$.

Equivalently, cutting along one diagonal gives two congruent triangles whose combined base is the long diagonal and whose combined height is the short one.

Either way the area is $\frac{1}{2} d_1 d_2 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot 24 = 120$.
